objective: Make the Cloud IaC module release-index gate fail closed when optional S3/GCS object-source rows omit local integrity and provider-specific pin metadata.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: The OpenTofu module-registry download endpoint returns a source location consumed by the CLI; release-index gates must not emit weak or unpinned source metadata.
OpenTofu module sources can reference archives and object-store-style sources including S3 and GCS patterns.
OpenTofu CLI credentials are configured outside module metadata; this slice rejects credential-like source metadata rather than embedding secrets.
S3 object versions are identified by version IDs; the release-index gate requires local version-id metadata for S3 object-source rows but does not execute S3 calls.
S3 object integrity is checksum-oriented; this ChangeSet binds object-source integrity metadata to the local archive SHA-256 only.
Cloud Storage object metadata includes generation values and checksums; the release-index gate requires local generation metadata for GCS object-source rows.
Cloud Storage supports generation preconditions; this slice records generation metadata locally and makes no live precondition-execution claim.
Artifact verification requires explicit evidence; signing/SLSA/VSA verification remains outside this local release-index gate slice.

red_tests.summary: The release-index gate accepted an S3 archive_source_location with only archive_source_integrity_sha256 and no provider-specific version-id pin before implementation.

implemented_claims: The Cloud IaC module release-index gate parses optional archive_source_location, archive_source_integrity_sha256, archive_source_version_id, and archive_source_generation fields from module rows.
Rows without archive_source_location reject orphan archive_source_integrity_sha256, archive_source_version_id, or archive_source_generation metadata.

Rows with archive_source_location require an s3::https:// or gcs::https:// location, reject whitespace/control/userinfo/query/fragment/credential-like markers, and require the location to end with the configured archive filename.
Rows with archive_source_location require archive_source_integrity_sha256 to be lowercase SHA-256 matching archive_sha256.
S3 object-source rows require safe archive_source_version_id and reject archive_source_generation.
GCS object-source rows require non-zero decimal archive_source_generation and reject archive_source_version_id.
explicit_non_claims: No live S3 or GCS read/write/list/head/precondition execution.
No object-store bucket provisioning, IAM policy enforcement, signed URL generation, CDN integration, or secret/credential management.
No deployed module registry endpoint, production auth/Cedar policy runtime, tenant identity, persistence, database adapter, TLS termination, measured SLO, DR, or capacity telemetry.
No signing, SLSA, VSA, provider runtime, tofu test/plan/apply, Argo CD/Kubernetes rollout, cloud provisioning, production readiness, or FD-001 tenant workload hosting.
No materialized production object-store release-index row; current live release-index rows remain local archive routes.
false_green_findings_closed: The release-index gate no longer ignores optional object-source fields in a way that would let unpinned S3/GCS module source rows pass gate validation before the app/runtime consumes them.
known_gaps: Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required is not claimed green.
Aggregate ./bin/oya gate run-all is not claimed green unless freshly rerun and proven.
Live object-store adapters, request precondition execution, signed module verification, production auth/Cedar, and deployment evidence remain future slices.
Repo-local release-index entries still use local archive routes; no production object-store release index has been materialized.

findings: Kept the slice narrow: release-index gate validation only, no fake live object-store implementation.
Moves object-backed module distribution toward immutable object/version addressing with deterministic local gate evidence and explicit non-claims.
Negative fixtures cover unpinned object-source metadata and integrity drift; the validator also rejects orphan pins, wrong-provider pins, unsafe source text, and malformed provider pins.
Existing local release-index rows without archive_source_location remain compatible; pin metadata becomes mandatory only when an object source is declared.
Focused release-index tests, fmt/check/clippy, governance gates, and full scoped Cloud IaC gate suite passed.

alternatives_named: Implement live S3/GCS object-store adapters now
Leave release-index gate unaware of optional object-source fields
Add local fail-closed release-index pin validation first
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Local fail-closed gate validation is the smallest honest hardening step after app-level object pin validation and before live object-store credentials/adapters exist.
rejected_reasons: Live adapters require buckets, IAM, credentials, precondition calls, and deployment evidence outside this slice.
Ignoring optional object-source fields creates a false-green path from release-index metadata to runtime serving.

findings: The gate rejects credential-like object-source metadata and binds optional object-source integrity back to archive_sha256 before release-index rows can pass.
Parser/gate-only validation adds no live object-store or network I/O path.
Version/generation metadata is explicit and locally gated; compliance-grade retention/precondition evidence remains non-claimed.
Local /artifacts/modules release-index entries remain valid because pin metadata is only required with archive_source_location.
Bad object-source metadata fails during release-index gate validation before runtime module-registry serving.
ChangeSet is tied to Oya VCS claim, source/tests, manifest/tasks, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain rows.
Used Oya VCS claim; avoided raw git/gh; read root hub and operating contract; kept /plan complementary-only; did not claim production/hyperscaler completion.
No new dependencies were introduced. Strict dependency-seam gate is run as closeout evidence.

review_findings: No critical/high issues found for the local release-index gate scope. Live object-store adapter/precondition verification remains an explicit gap.

Scoped retired-vocabulary used a temporary corpus containing the claimed files because the gate accepts directory corpus roots and broader oya-dev-cli directories contain unrelated pre-existing retired vocabulary drift.
